newsitem.title: FRANCE: France creates task force to fight EU budget fraud.
newsitem.headline: France creates task force to fight EU budget fraud.

text.p: The French government stepped up the fight against fraudulent use of European Commission budget funds with the establishment on Wednesday of a special domestic task force.

"Fraud is unacceptable in all its forms but I think fraud in the Community budget provokes particular resentment from our citizens," European Affairs Minister Michel Barnier said as he announced the creation of the anti-fraud task force ICLAF.

He said the Commission's 1995 annual report estimated that around 1.1 billion European currency units ($1.4 billion), or nearly 1.5 percent of its budget, had been wrongly diverted. "That's a lot," Barnier said.
The Commission in 1994 declared the fight against fraud a priority and created the European UCLAF anti-fraud coordination force.
The new French task force will monitor the activities of French agencies involved in fighting fraud and will be France's link with the UCLAF, Budget Minister Alain Lamassoure said.

Given the budgetary rigour of European governments straining to meet the Maastricht criteria for monetary union, the campaign to stamp out fraud at the European Union level is more important than ever, he said.

"Over the past three years, the total amount of fraud and irregularities detected by the Commission and its member states has grown more than fivefold, rising from 204 million Ecus in 1992 to more than 1.1 billion in 1995," he said. He said the rise reflected the success of the anti-fraud campaign.
Lamassoure said France contributes 18 percent of the European Union budget, while around 16 percent is spent in France.
The European Union's Council of Ministers voted in July to cut the budget for 1997 by 0.3 percent. ($1=.7989 European Currency Unit)
